title: Change approval scenarios and forensic checklist for private deployments
content:
Context and intent:
This is a working playbook for the Private product: it defines realistic change approval scenarios, the minimum evidence we capture for each approval tier, and a compact forensic checklist operators should use if an approval later needs to be audited or rolled back. The focus is customer-managed networking + operator actions that affect control-plane connectivity, credentialing, and edge peering.

Why this doc exists (short):
- We keep getting ad hoc asks about what constitutes ‘sufficient evidence’ for network/operator changes in customer-managed VPCs.
- We need a lightweight, repeatable checklist that SREs, platform engineers, and customer operators can use to avoid over- or under-collecting logs.
- This also feeds into Compliance: a consistent audit artifact model reduces friction in SOC reviews.

Goals:
- Define approval tiers mapped to change risk and who must sign-off.
- Specify minimal set of logs, snapshots, and attestations required per tier.
- Offer rapid forensic checklist for incidents that reference those changes.
- Keep operational cost bounded: sampling and TTLs are part of the design.

Scope (what’s in/out):
- IN: customer-managed networking handshakes (peering, route updates), operator-initiated credential rotations, control-plane config pushes, edge operator runbooks (onboarding/eviction).
- OUT: hosted model config changes, non-networking-only UI tweaks, app-level data model migrations (handled by other teams).

Personas: who cares
- Customer Network Admin (CNA): initiates VPC peering and provides attestation.
- Redwood Edge Operator: performs operator-visible steps (handshake, cert install, healthcheck).
- SRE/Oncall Reviewer: validates evidence, escalates when discrepancies.
- Compliance Reviewer / Auditor: retrospectively checks artifacts.

Change classification and approval tiers (high level):
- Tier 0 — Informational / Non-impacting: metadata updates that do not change connectivity (e.g., contact info). No approval required; auto-log.
- Tier 1 — Low-risk operational: non-routing certificate renewals, agent version bumps that do not require downtime. Routed to CNA + Edge Operator acknowledgement. Evidence: cert fingerprint + rollout manifest.
- Tier 2 — Moderate-risk: route additions, new peer setup, control-plane ACL edits that can change reachability. Requires CNA attestation + 1 Redwood approver (Edge Lead). Evidence bundle (see below).
- Tier 3 — High-risk / Breaking changes: peering teardown, route deletions, credential revocation, inbound firewall policy changes. Requires CNA attestation + 2 Redwood approvers (Edge Lead + SRE manager) + optional customer change window.

Approval gates matrix (concise):
- Trigger event -> Required approvers -> Evidence produced -> Sampling policy
- New peer creation -> CNA + Edge Operator -> API handshake log, mutual TLS cert chain, peering policy JSON, control-plane connectivity test (before/after) -> store 100% for 30d
- Route insertion -> CNA attestation + 1 approver -> BGP session snapshot, route table diff, simulated reachability test -> store 50% for 14d, sample remaining 10% for 90d
- Certificate rotation -> Edge Operator only (if non-breaking) -> cert fingerprint + k/v metadata -> store 30d
- Emergency credential revoke -> CNA ack (post-fact allowed) + SRE manager -> revocation invocation logs, affected sessions list, rollback steps -> store 365d

Evidence bundle (minimum fields each artifact must include):
- Who: actor identity (email + team), auth method (SAML/SSO/cli-key), request id
- What: change diff (pre/post), exact API calls or CLI commands run, PR/Change-id if applicable
- When: UTC timestamp (ISO8601) of request + wallclock time of execution phase
- Where: src IP (customer), edge node id, control-plane region
- How validated: smoke test results (pass/fail), captured tcpdump/traceroute short trace, application-level healthcheck results
- Declaration: CNA attestation statement (checkbox text) signed with SSO assertion id or explicit PR link

Format and storage semantics (practical):
- Primary evidence format: compact JSONL artifacts (one line per artifact) — preferred because easy to index and version.
- Secondary artifacts: tarball of diagnostic files (pcap snippets, route table screenshots) for Tier 2/3 only. Tarballs must contain a manifest.json (flat key-value lines).
- All artifacts for Tier >=2 must be uploaded to customer-designated S3 or Redwood escrow bucket (depends on contract).
- Retention buckets: 30d / 90d / 365d policies above are starting points; product should expose retention override only by legal/contract.

Forensic checklist (quick runbook when a change is suspected to cause outage):
1) Identify the most recent change id affecting the impacted edge/control-plane (use request id).
2) Pull evidence bundle (JSONL). Confirm actor identity and match to scheduled change window.
3) Validate pre/post route diff for accidental deletion or prefix overlap.
4) Check mutual TLS handshake logs for certificate mismatch or expired chain.
5) Run live traceroute from edge node to customer endpoint; compare to saved trace.
6) If traffic blackholed: inspect iptables/edge ACL snapshot in tarball.
7) If credential revocation: enumerate active sessions from session-store snapshot.
8) Produce an incident addendum: timeline + snapshot pointers + recommended rollback.

Sampling policy rationale (cost vs. auditability):
- Full capture for any Tier 3 change and for initial onboarding peering events (first 90d).
- Deterministic sampling for Tier 2: first request include full tarball; subsequent similar requests sample at 1-in-5 for 90d.
- Tier 1 mostly summarized metadata only (no pcap) unless operator flags anomaly.

On-call decision flow for approval disputes (short):
- If CNA contest: check SSO assertion timestamp and verify signature. If SSO missing, escalate to Edge Lead.
- If evidence mismatch: reproduce connectivity test in a sandbox infra mirror (instructions below).
- If rollback needed and CNA unavailable: follow emergency rollback playbook (requires SRE manager signoff).

Example scenarios (illustrative):
A) Customer adds a new peer for analytics replicate. Tier 2. Evidence: peering API logs, TLS chain, BGP session OK, simulated reachability. Approver: Edge Lead. Post-deploy sample storage: 90d.
B) Operator rotates agent cert across 200 edge nodes. Tier 1. Evidence: rotation manifest + cert fingerprints. Rolling window: staged-in-two-batches; sampling: manifest stored 30d.
C) Customer requests deletion of an existing route that currently carries production traffic. Tier 3. Evidence: route diff + rollback plan + customer SLA window. Approvers: CNA + Edge Lead + SRE manager. Must schedule maintenance window.

Implementation notes for engineers (actionable bullets):
- Add a standard JSONL schema: {request_id, actor, actor_type, change_type, pre_hash, post_hash, artifacts_url[], timestamp, smoke_result}. Keep schema stable for 2 quarters.
- Expose an API endpoint /audit/evidence/{request_id} that returns signed manifest and pre-signed artifact URLs (expiry 24h).
- Integrate SSO assertion id into each approver decision record (authn traceability).
- Add CLI flag --approval-evidence to edge-operator agent so operator action automatically bundles required artifacts.
- For customers who choose escrow: support configurable S3 paths and object encryption (KMS key id per customer).

Dependencies / integrations:
- Controls: SSO (Okta), audit storage (Redwood escrow S3), ticketing (JIRA PD project), CI link (github PR id).
- Observability: console needs a timeline view with links to evidence bundles; infra to index JSONL.

Open questions / trade-offs (short list):
- Long-term storage cost for full pcaps: could we limit pcap snippets to the first 5 minutes of change?
- How to surface CNA attestation in workflows where the customer lacks SSO integration? (email attestations are weaker.)
- Should we encrypt manifest fields for PII-sensitive metadata (src IP) by default?

Next steps (owner/action):
- Ava: iterate acceptance criteria and convert JSONL schema to a proto (due 2026-03-01).
- Miguel: prototype /audit/evidence endpoint and sample manifest (due 2026-03-15).
- Priya: draft console timeline wireframe linking evidence bundles (due 2026-03-10).
- Jules: update onboarding checklist to require CNA attestation template (due 2026-03-08).

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally pragmatic — we prioritize a small set of deterministic artifacts rather than bloated capture.
- Look for places we can automate evidence generation from existing infra (agent logs, BGP monitor).

Appendix: minimal JSON snippet example (single-line):
{"request_id":"pd-20260218-00091","actor":"cna@acme.inc","change_type":"peer-create","artifacts_url":["s3://escrow/pd-20260218-00091/manifest.jsonl"],"timestamp":"2026-02-18T21:34:12Z","smoke_result":"pass"}

End of draft.
Comments: I expect a lot of bikeshedding on exact retention numbers; recommended to treat those as negotiable knobs in product config.
